subject: Effort information when using hair traps

messages.author: 500d98abd0834d18
messages.subject: Effort information when using hair traps
parts:
Hi all,
I would have a question regarding SCR modelling, and I thought you might help.
With camera traps, when a camera does not work, but an animal passes by, not accounting for the malfunctioning of the device would, of course, lead to an underestimation of g0. 
And this has to be accounted for when using any kind of detector. 
I will get a dataset with data from hair samples collected at sticks that were lured with valerian scent at the start of each week. That means the sticks get less appealing in the following days, similar to a trap that stops functioning, so to say. 
I was thinking I could arbitrarily set a day after which I consider the detector (the stick) as no longer able to attract (0 instead of 1).

Thanks!

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Effort information when using hair traps
parts:
Two points:
1. In your case the 'usage' mechanism seems unduly arbitrary. Why not fit a temporal trend (~T) or equivalently use a time covariate?
2. Simulations suggest temporal variation in detection is not a big deal (Sollmann 2024; SECR book Ch 6)

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Effort information when using hair traps
parts: No, there's no connection to 'usage'. 'usage' and g0~T can be used together if, for example, there are days when some traps were not set. g0~T applies to captures at the traps that were set.
